extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and performers studying craft
extracted.subtask_description: A synthesis of Marc Maron's recurring craft observations for stand-up comics and performers, emphasizing presence, specificity, processing painful material, repetition, listening, and practical habits like recording sets. Intended as a pragmatic checklist to evaluate and develop stage material and performance discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy is a way of NOT having a feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is a way of NOT having a feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat comedy as a mechanism for working through emotions; this frames material as a means of processing rather than merely entertaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: The funny is in the specific, fucked-up detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The funny is in the specific, fucked-up detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize concrete, embarrassing, or idiosyncratic specifics in premises and punchlines rather than vague statements; specificity is where humor often lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be in the moment — audience senses inauthenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience can smell it when you're not in the moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence matters: avoid performing on autopilot. If you aren't genuinely engaged, the audience detects it and the joke will suffer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage time is the primary metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage time is the only thing that matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize getting onstage regularly; practice and exposure to different rooms are the essential drivers of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk what you can't talk about
rubrics_metrics.description: "What you can't talk about is what you HAVE to talk about."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard, taboo, or painful subjects often contain the most vital material. Expect discomfort early in the process but prioritize authenticity over avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect early attempts to be unfunny (processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first attempt at hard material will be unfunny — it's processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat initial performances of difficult material as processing steps rather than finished jokes; don't judge final potential on first tries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition/metabolism produces humor
rubrics_metrics.description: The fifth attempt may be funny — by then the comic has metabolized it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterate material multiple times (Maron cites around five tries) — repetition allows emotional processing and comedic refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-up is metabolic work / ongoing process
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of stand-up is metabolism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View comedy as an ongoing internal transformation: writing and performing are processes that change your relationship to material over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft emerges from genuine listening
rubrics_metrics.description: WTF demonstrates that craft can emerge from genuine listening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interviews and onstage interactions, listening can produce comedic opportunities; being responsive can create authentic comedic beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual surprise produces the funniest moments
rubrics_metrics.description: The funniest moments in interviews are when both speakers are surprised together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for moments of shared discovery with audience or interlocutor rather than a one-way joke delivery; spontaneity and genuine surprise heighten humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find jokes in the moment rather than bringing them
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't bring a joke; find one in the moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to improvisation and emergent humor from interactions rather than rigidly forcing prepared bits in every situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value bombing as subject and teacher
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombing more than killing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professionals discuss bombing — both as a frequent reality and as a learning opportunity. Treat failures as useful data rather than shameful endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze specific failed premises
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific premises that didn't work, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissect what failed and why at a granular level (premise, wording, delivery, context) to refine material; pros discuss failed premises openly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from different rooms and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rooms (NYC vs LA vs the road) and what they teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different venues and audiences teach different lessons; use varied stage environments to test and adapt material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid toxic comparison; commit to process
rubrics_metrics.description: The toxicity of comparison; the necessity of process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't measure progress by comparing to others; focus on your own iterative process and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate 'funny' from 'comedian' — discipline matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Funny is a quality. Comedian is a discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being inherently funny is not enough; cultivate the habits, persistence, and craft to sustain comedy under real-world pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain comedy under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: The comedian sustains the funny under the pressure of stage, time, and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on reliability and endurance: can you produce the funny consistently in adverse or pressured conditions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment and resilience are required
rubrics_metrics.description: Most "funny" people can't be comedians; the work is unrelenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that successful comedians commit to an often-grueling process; resilience and continual labor separate hobbyists from professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke metabolizing something real?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke metabolizing something real?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the material reflects genuine processing of lived experience or emotion; authenticity of transformation increases comedic potency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you done the joke five times yet?
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you done the joke five times yet?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a rough iteration-count heuristic (Maron suggests five performances) before expecting material to land; track repetition as part of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you listening to the room or pushing through it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you listening to the room or pushing through it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether your performance adapts to audience feedback and energy, or whether you're rigidly forcing material despite cues to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the specific, embarrassing detail present?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the specific, embarrassing detail in the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure jokes contain the pinpointed specific or embarrassing detail that gives the premise life; lacking specifics often makes bits generic and weaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you a comedian today, or just a funny person hoping?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you a comedian today, or just a funny person hoping?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as an accountability check: are you practicing the discipline (preparing, testing, showing up), or merely relying on innate charm?

rubrics_metrics.name: Record the set and listen back
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you record the set and listen back?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make recording and review a habit: listening to recordings provides objective data on pacing, wording, and audience reaction to refine material.
